published_prior_art.cite: GabrielSachsSjolander2025: Results 1 and 3 give low-cardinality contrast bounds; SongGuoChanRichardson2024: arbitrary-cardinality characterization assumes exclusion at every exposure level.
BalkePearl1997: sharp binary-IV response-type bounds for the ATE.
SongGuoChanRichardson2024: fully excluded categorical IV model; it does not give this saturated-versus-common-off-target certificate.
Blackwell1953 supplies experiment-comparison machinery but not a parameter-dependent off-target allocation nuisance minimax equality.
SongGuoChanRichardson2024: finite-sample KL projection is for the fully excluded full alphabet, not the target-only saturated quotient.
Hoffman1952 and Li1993 provide generic polyhedral sensitivity, not the quotient-IV compatible-fiber consequence.
LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025 gives margin/smoothing inference for covariate-assisted binary-IV bounds, not this quotient-invariant local lower bound.
Gafarov2025 gives regularized affine-model inference but not the exact local minimax phase diagram and adaptive attainment problem for this target-IV quotient.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Result 1 treats a two-level IV with two target well-defining exposure levels and one ill-defining or contaminated level; Result 3 treats a three-level IV with two target levels and the analogous third-level relaxation.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 11–13, Assumptions 1–2 and Theorem 1; pp. 25–27, Section 6 and Theorem 4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes exclusion for every categorical exposure level, characterizes the joint law of all exposure potential outcomes, and gives simultaneous finite-sample coverage for linear functionals through a KL-based convex program.
Theorem 1 gives the alphabet-generic polynomial expression bounding the multinomial empirical-relative-entropy moment generating function.
The paper develops a novel margin condition for parametric-rate influence-function estimation of IV bounds and smooth approximations of nonsmooth bounds.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5 and 12–13, support-value setup and regularity/dual-multiplicity discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies sharp identified sets in affine models, support values, regularity conditions, and regularization to address dual multiplicity.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a corollary explicitly embedding Gabriel et al.'s Result 1 and Result 3 regimes into the quotient model, including the exact map from their third level to the collapsed star cell.
State a practical algorithm and complexity bound for constructing the right inverse and optimizing the reduced fiber, rather than only reporting response-type column counts.

Sharpen the kink OEQ by naming a concrete two-vertex dual-tie skeleton family and the proposed local scaling, so its active-cone frontier can be distinguished more directly from Gafarov's generic regularization framework.

recommended_next_step: Advance this field-tier quotient kernel to Stage 0, retaining Theorem 1 as the headline and treating the binary reduction as validation rather than novelty.
